source.title: Batch Normalization Biases Residual Blocks Towards the Identity Function in Deep Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test accuracy across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and finds that the effect depends on normalization, regularization, and dataset; its ImageNet results also show batch normalization remaining stable as batch size rises.
record.gate_note: The study does not test fitting random labels, widening past interpolation, optimizer comparisons, dropout versus no dropout as a general intervention, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Batch-size figures are described qualitatively in the text; cited prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Fixed-epoch batch-size sweeps test V5 in additional residual-network settings. Table 2 also tests V6 through matched Fixup and SkipInit comparisons with and without dropout. This study is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase omits the central conclusion and overgeneralizes the batch-size trend. The authors conclude that batch normalization primarily enables deep residual-network training by biasing residual blocks toward identity at initialization, a benefit recovered by SkipInit. Its larger stable learning rates help at large batches but offer little practical benefit at small batches. Normalization also regularizes; alternative regularization can sometimes exceed its accuracy. The statement that accuracy never improves with batch size pertains to the fixed-ghost-batch Section 3 sweeps, whereas full-minibatch normalization has an intermediate optimum.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares batch normalization and residual-branch initialization methods across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets; it does not reproduce the named large-batch studies' full recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depends on batch size, normalization or initialization method, dataset, and whether batch statistics use a fixed ghost batch or the full mini-batch; added regularization changes some comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularized SkipInit outperforms batch normalization at very small CIFAR batch sizes and can remain competitive at moderately large sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternative initialization and regularization packages can match or exceed batch normalization in some batch-size regimes.

record.problems: The ImageNet table reports a single run at each learning rate. Several batch-size results are available only as qualitative figure descriptions in the supplied text. Learning rates are tuned on the test set for CIFAR experiments, as the authors acknowledge.
record.rows_left_out: None. Extracted the text-described batch-size trends and all ResNet50-V2 Table 2 validation-accuracy entries; exact values for figure-only trends were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Held-out comparisons between convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and sensitivity to optimizer tuning.
Language models; longer-training remedies; controlled ablations of warmup and learning-rate scaling. ImageNet uses warmup and tuned learning rates but does not isolate their causal contributions.
Fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus matched random removals.

missing.what: All Table 7 ResNet50-V1 batch-size results: batch normalization 75.6/92.5, 75.3/92.4, 75.4/92.4; Fixup 74.4/91.6, 74.4/91.7, 72.4/90.3; Regularized SkipInit 70.0/89.2, 68.4/87.8, 68.2/87.9; with scalar bias 75.2/92.4, 74.9/92.0, 70.8/89.6, at batch sizes 256, 1024 and 4096 respectively.

The unnormalized, non-SkipInit CIFAR-10 batch-size sweep and the explicit finding that batch normalization shifts the accuracy-degradation threshold to substantially larger batches. Existing R1-R2 omit this direct comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 values are accurate, but most original states used cross-method comparisons instead of the within-method contrasts V5 requires. Rows serving multiple versions have their version-specific states explained in problem. ImageNet has one run per learning rate; CIFAR learning rates are selected on test accuracy and reported averages retain the best runs. No absent or reversed result warrants a challenges label against the qualified versions supplied.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Language models; training longer, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and some other cited recipe adaptations are discussed or cited but not tested as alternatives in the batch-size sweeps.
Dropout's effect as described in the version; dropout appears only as part of Regularized SkipInit comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.note: Qualitative result; exact plotted values are not given in the text.
